messages.author: fde4048c840328bf
messages.subject: Using "block" operator in matrices
parts:
Hi all! 

I have a question about the use of the block operator, since I think that I am not sure how to use it properly (and I get parser errors).

Let us suppose that I have to build a matrix of parameters A, which is 3x3, and that I have other vector of parameters, which is declared as a matrix B, 1x3. As a simple example, I want that (using R notation) A[3,1:2] = B[1,2:3]. I tried to do this,

block(A,3,1,1,2) <- block(B,1,2,1,3), but I always get a parser error,

EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=39, column=9

        block(A,k,1,1,(k-1))    <- block(B,1,index,1,(index+k-2));
        ^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning: integer division implicitly rounds to integer. Found int division: (K * (K - 1)) / 2
 Positive values rounded down, negative values rounded up or down in platform-dependent way.
binary infix operator <= with functional interpretation logical_lt requires arguments or primitive type (int or real), found left type=matrix, right arg type=matrix; no matches for function name="logical_lt"
    arg 0 type=matrix
    arg 1 type=matrix
available function signatures for logical_lt:
0.  logical_lt(int, int) : int
1.  logical_lt(int, real) : int
2.  logical_lt(real, int) : int
3.  logical_lt(real, real) : int
Parser expecting: "}"

If you want to know exactly how I build the matrix, it is, which ends up being the lower triangular elements of a matrix KxK

    int           index;
    index       <- 1;

    for(k in 2:K){
    
        block(A,k,1,1,(k-1))    <- block(B,1,index,1,(index+k-2));
        index                   <- index + k - 1;
    }

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using "block" operator in matrices
parts:
I'm afraid we don't allow block operations
on the left-hand side of assignments. It's on the
to-do list, but not supported yet. So the only thing
you can do is a loop.

Sorry the error message is so cryptic. There's already
an issue filed about it and I hope to fix it before
releasing 2.0.

- Bob

P.S. The problem is that when the parser reads this line:

block(A,k,1,1,(k-1)) <- block(B,1,index,1,(index+k-2));

it can't parse it as an assignment, because only variables
with indices are allowed on the LHS of an assignment. So it
tries to parse an expression and gets this far:

operand 1: block(A,k,1,1,(k-1))
operation: <
operand 2: operation: -
operand: block(B,1,index,1,(index+k-2))

It then tries to be helpful by telling you that you can't
apply the logical less-than operator to two matrices.
Now calling the < operation "logical_lt" is doubly confusing, because
"logical_lt" is an internal name we shouldn't be reporting back
to users. (There's a similar issue some of the indexing
messages, which report on an internal representation of getters.)
